text:
anya: Quick heads-up — seeing function-call JSON failures on prod for the new gptx-13b fp8/gptq mixes.

michael: Ugh, what errors? stacktraces?

anya: Clients report tool args arriving as a flat string instead of an array. e.g. tool call payload -> "args": "[\"file.pdf\"]" instead of ["file.pdf"]. JSON.parse fails downstream.

devon: That's usually a serialization double-encode. Is it only on quantized endpoints?

anya: Looks like it correlates with AWQ/INT8 variants. Non-quantized FP16 endpoints don't show it.

sylvia: Any recent runtime changes? KV cache warps, kernel reorder?

anya: We rolled a micropatch that switches to packed KV layout earlier today — could be related. Repro steps below.

anya: Repro snippet:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-13b-awq-int8","input":"<sys>: call_tool compute \\n{\"name\":\"pdf_extractor\",\"args\":[\"file.pdf\"]}" }'
```

michael: I ran it in sandbox, saw: `TypeError: JSON.parse: unexpected token \" at 1` with payload "args":"[\"file.pdf\"]". Here's the raw response snippet:
```
{ "tool_call": { "name":"pdf_extractor", "args":"[\"file.pdf\"]" } }
```

devon: Hm. Could be that the structured-output post-processor is stringifying for quant variants because of some tokenization-induced escapes.

raj: Hypothesis: tokenization merge for AWQ causes function-call markers to get split across model outputs, and our postprocessing tries to reassemble and ends up double-quoting. Need to check streaming boundary logic.

sylvia: Agreed. Also check truncation thresholds. If streaming chunk cuts inside JSON, our joiner might wrap segments in quotes to preserve literal tokens.

anya: I ran a quick local test toggling streaming off — then payload is correct. So streaming + quantized path seems necessary for failure.

devon: Action items:
- devon: add unit test covering streaming chunk boundary + funcall decoding for AWQ/INT8 (inference-codec tests)
- michael: collect 50 failing trace ids from prod, include model variant and kernel selection
- sylvia: rollback packed KV on one canary, see if failure rate drops
- raj: instrument streaming assembler to log whether it inserted extra quotes when concatenating

quant-bot: Automated check results for gptx-13b-awq-int8 on streaming assembler: 14/100 structured-output samples showed stringified arrays. Full log gist: https://ci.redwood/gists/qa-178250

michael: Will upload sample traces to the incident channel.

anya: For immediate mitigation, can we route quantized streaming requests through non-streaming path for tool-calling endpoints? That should be a cheap temporary fix.

devon: Yes we can add a feature-flagged routing rule in the runtime router. I'll open PR and enable for canary.

sylvia: Also add a quick sanitizer: when postprocessor sees a string that matches /^\[.*\]$/ try JSON.parse and coerce into array instead of failing. Defensive but OK short-term.

raj: Long-term we need to ensure codec is aware of token boundaries and preserves structural tokens across quant kernels.

anya: Thanks team. Please drop updates in this thread. :thumbsup:

devon: PR #4321 opened: runtime: route quantized streaming -> blocking decode for /v1/call_tool (canary). link: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4321

michael: Uploaded traces: s3://redwood-logs/prod/traces/17825/trace-*.ndjson

sylvia: Can confirm canary saw 0 failures in 2k requests so far. :tada:

anya: Great. We'll monitor and decide on full rollout after 24h.
